## Further reading {#sec-further-reading}

These books and articles treat sets and the logic behind them in more depth.

- @devlin1993joy
  is an undergraduate introduction to axiomatic set theory.
  It covers the axioms of set theory, ordinals, and cardinals,
  which go well beyond the countable sets and functions in these notes.
- @halmos1974naive
  is a short, informal treatment of the same axioms,
  covering relations, functions, families of sets, and cardinal numbers.
- @enderton2001logic
  is a standard introduction to mathematical logic.
  Its first chapter collects the facts about sets, relations, and functions
  that the later chapters use.
- @barkerplummer2011language
  teaches propositional and first-order logic,
  the language behind statements such as "for every set $A$ there exists...".

-   @wikipedia_set_mathematics --- sets, with the naive and axiomatic views

-   @wikipedia_set_builder_notation --- set-builder notation

-   @wikipedia_interval_mathematics --- intervals and their endpoints

-   @wikipedia_subset --- subsets and the symbol conventions

-   @wikipedia_empty_set --- the empty set

-   @wikipedia_vacuous_truth --- vacuous truth

-   @wikipedia_family_of_sets --- families of sets

-   @wikipedia_index_set --- index sets

-   @wikipedia_indexed_family --- indexed families

-   @wikipedia_union_set_theory --- unions of sets

-   @wikipedia_intersection_set_theory --- intersections of sets

-   @wikipedia_complement_set_theory --- complements and set differences

-   @wikipedia_de_morgans_laws --- De Morgan's laws

-   @wikipedia_ordered_pair --- ordered pairs

-   @wikipedia_cartesian_product --- Cartesian products

-   @wikipedia_extended_real_number_line --- the extended real number line
